anchors.paper_title: MNE-BIDS: Organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format and facilitating their analysis
anchors.paper_venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
anchors.reason: The paper describes MNE-BIDS, a general standard for organizing electrophysiological data into the BIDS format, which is a technical specification/tool, not a paper introducing the MEG-SCANS dataset.

anchors.paper_title: MEG-BIDS, the brain imaging data structure extended to magnetoencephalography
anchors.reason: The paper proposes MEG-BIDS, a data structure standard for organizing MEG data, which is a technical specification/methodology used for data sharing, not a paper introducing the MEG-SCANS dataset.

metadata.methods_description: MEG data were recorded from 24 German-speaking participants during an approximately one-hour auditory experiment involving audiobooks, OLSA sentences at varying speech intelligibility levels, and chirp stimuli. Data collection included raw and MaxFiltered MEG recordings, pre- and post-session empty-room MEG recordings, structural MRI scans, and behavioral audiogram/SRT results. Auxiliary MISC channels captured audio and instructor microphone signals at 1000 Hz.
